subject: Post-call: Capacity priming simulation & ops plan
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@brightentry.com>, BrightEntry Eng <eng@brightentry.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Capacity priming simulation & ops plan

Hi Alice (and team),

Thanks again for the call — good alignment on the high-level SLOs. Below is a short recap plus proposed next steps so we can run a priming/simulation that will validate Redwood's burst behavior for your workload. I attached a small simulation template and an SLO-readme that explains metrics we’ll capture.

Key requirements you called out:
- P95 generation latency target: <= 150 ms for standard prompt completions (no heavy tool calls).
- Streaming: first-byte streaming latency <= 100 ms for token streaming; client needs token-by-token as responses arrive.
- Concurrency: typical steady-state concurrency ~200 requests, with burst peaks up to ~800 concurrent requests for 3–7 minutes during product launches.
- Tolerance for queued requests: up to 20s in narrow situations, but ideally keep tail <5s.

Assumptions we made on the call (please correct):
- You will run the simulation from the nat'ed test agents in us-west-2.
- Sample traffic will be the 10-minute window you shared (we asked for an anonymized preview).
- Test should include both streaming and non-streaming endpoints.

Proposed simulation plan (short):
1) Dry run (15m): small ramp to 200 concurrent, verify telemetry, ensure client streaming handshake passes. Owner: BrightEntry + Redwood SRE (Marcus).
2) Priming run (30m): emulate the launch ramp to 800 concurrency with a 5-minute plateau. Observe warm-pool behavior and cold start counts. Owner: Redwood infra (Marcus).
3) Chaos probe (10m): throttle a subset of nodes to see fallback latency and queueing behavior. Owner: Redwood infra; operations will coordinate.
4) Post-run analysis: deliver histogram of P50/P95/P99, streaming first-byte times, and KV-cache hit ratio. Owner: Redwood (Tessa + Marcus).

Immediate asks for BrightEntry (before we schedule):
- Please upload anonymized traffic preview (1–2 MB) or confirm we can use the sample you mentioned.
- Confirm whether you'd prefer Hosted API or a short Dedicated trial for the test (Dedicated will reduce cold-start noise).
- Confirm timezone windows where a 1-hour test is acceptable for your on-call.

Attachments: burst_sim_template.csv (ramp schedule + request mix), slo_readme.pdf (metrics definitions).

Suggested slots: Wed 4/22 09:00-12:00 PT or Thu 4/23 13:00-16:00 PT. If those don't work, share 2 options.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate resources on our side once you confirm the slot.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference runtime

Tessa — thanks for the clear notes. This looks good and mirrors what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- We attached a small sample (brightentry_traffic_preview.json) with obfuscated user ids; that file contains the 10-minute window we referenced. Please treat as internal-only.
- Our infrastructure is currently hybrid: most traffic originates from our eu-west-1 region but we can route test traffic from us-west-2 agents as long as you note the egress path. For the real launch we’ll use eu region but for priming we want to prove the scaling model in us-west-2 first.
- Regarding Dedicated vs Hosted: we prefer Hosted for the initial test to avoid procurement delays, but would like a follow-up run on Dedicated if the Hosted run shows >5% cold-start variance.

We can do Wed 4/22 09:30-11:00 PT. Ops will be available and I’ll put Marcus in touch with our on-call lead (contact attached in the sample).

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Capacity priming simulation & ops plan

Thanks — copying a few technical notes / asks so we can lock the simulation parameters. A few items for BrightEntry ops: please confirm or provide the following before Wed: 

1) Traffic mix: % short (<=32 tokens) vs long (>512 tokens). The preview looks ~75% short, 25% long. Confirm.
2) Percent streaming traffic: ~30% of requests will be streaming token-by-token.
3) Auth/keepalive: do clients re-open connections per request or reuse persistent HTTP/2 streams? Persistent streams will materially reduce cold-path overhead.
4) Error handling: what rate of synthetic errors should we inject (0.1% baseline) during the chaos probe?

Test parameters we’ll run (proposed):
- Dry run: ramp to 200 concurrent over 5m, hold 10m.
- Priming: linear ramp from 200 -> 800 over 120s, hold 5m, then drop to 300.
- Warm pool policy: pre-warm target = 25% of peak (200 instances) with 45s probe for readyness.
- Scale-up target: median scale-up time goal < 20s, 95th < 45s.
- Queueing: allow max queue 20s but aim to keep 95th < 5s (we’ll measure).

Telemetry we need (please provide access or a sample export):
- request_id, timestamp, latency_ms, downstream_http_status, token_count, stream_first_byte_ms.

If those sound good, we’ll bring the priming harness and run on Wed 4/22 09:30 PT. I’ll provision test pools and share the runbook link.

—Marcus
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
